desc:
The alternating sum of a non-empty subarray nums[l..r] is nums[l] - nums[l+1] + nums[l+2] - ...: signs alternate and the first element always has a plus sign.

Return the largest alternating sum over all non-empty subarrays.

Examples: [3, 1, 5] gives 7 (3 - 1 + 5); [1, 5, -1] gives 6 (the subarray [5, -1], 5 - (-1)).
hints: The sign of an element depends on its distance from the start of the chosen subarray, not on its index in the array.
Keep two values for subarrays ending at i: plus, where nums[i] carries a plus sign (it is at an even offset), and minus, where it carries a minus sign.

plus = nums[i] + max(0, minus_prev) (either start fresh at i or continue a run whose last sign was minus). minus = plus_prev - nums[i] (the run must already exist). The answer is the best value of either.
editorial: Think of the subarray as a chain whose signs go +, -, +, ... Let plus[i] be the best total of a chain that ends at i with nums[i] being added, and minus[i] the best total of a chain ending at i with nums[i] being subtracted. A chain whose last element is added either begins at i (total nums[i]) or continues from a chain whose last element was subtracted. A chain whose last element is subtracted can only come from a chain whose last element was added, because the first sign is always plus.
So plus[i] = nums[i] + max(0, minus[i-1]) and minus[i] = plus[i-1] - nums[i]. Take the maximum of every plus and minus. It is Kadane on two interleaved states. O(n) time, O(1) space.
solution:
def maxAlternatingSubarraySum(nums):
    NEG = float("-inf")
    plus = nums[0]
    minus = NEG
    best = plus
    for x in nums[1:]:
        new_plus = x + max(0, minus)
        new_minus = plus - x
        plus, minus = new_plus, new_minus
        best = max(best, plus, minus)
    return best
